analysis:
The PR adds only documentation: changelog.d/serving-stalls.md (new) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (load-gate flowchart at lines 298-299, new reclaim paragraph after line 337). No executable code is included. The Swift implementation (KVPoolReclaimer, CBv2RetainedKVSegments, WholeMacServiceBudget.performIfIdle, GlobalKVCacheBudget.directChargeRefusalSignal, load gates) was not supplied, so its behavior is unverified.

The documented behavior and the threat model:
- Retained free KV segments: up to 1/8 of the slot grant, at most 2 GiB, kept across requests. They are reinstalled for the next admission instead of being newly allocated and zero-filled. The doc says new segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages, so reinstalled segments are reused without a fresh device fill. This touches T-028 (residual inference data in GPU memory / KV cache after a request completes, TB-007). The cross-request retention window is new, and it is bounded at 30 s of engine idleness. The changelog does not say whether a retained segment is zeroed or scrubbed before reinstall for a different consumer. If segments are reused without zeroing, stale KV from a previous tenant could be exposed to the next request, but the paged pool's page tables and sequence lengths normally bound reads to a request's own pages. A provider operator already has plaintext access (ADV-001, T-014), so this is not a new provider-side exposure, and I cannot verify it from docs alone. Recommend the next pass check that retained and reinstalled segments are either zeroed or only readable through request-owned page mappings.
- Retained segments are uncommitted (no ledger charge). The doc says they are released on pressure and counted as reclaimable by the load gates, so this is an availability/accounting matter rather than a security issue. Whether the ledger and cap invariants still hold is unverified.
- The idle-sweep and load-gate changes affect only availability and are rollback-controlled by DARKBLOOM_TTFT_* env vars. There is no change to the wire protocol, attestation, keys, authorization, or prefix-cache encryption (T-041).

No finding is supported by the supplied evidence. needs_deeper_review is set to true only for the unverified segment-reuse scrubbing contract.
